_doc: USER-EDITABLE seed source registry for Model Radar. Edit this file directly to add, remove, or retag sources — it is data, not code. Each source's stance_hint is a DEFAULT only: extraction may override the stance per evidence item (e.g. a practitioner video reading a lab's benchmark table yields a lab_claim evidence item). stance_hint must be one of the dossier-schema.json stance enum values: lab_claim | independent_eval | practitioner_take. TO ADD A SOURCE: append an object to 'sources' with a unique id (lowercase-hyphenated), kind ('lab_page' for a lab's release/news page, 'youtube_channel' for a channel), name, stance_hint, and a note explaining why it's worth harvesting. For lab_page also set url and lab. For youtube_channel also set channel_id and rss_url in the keyless form https://www.youtube.com/feeds/videos.xml?channel_id=<CHANNEL_ID> (same convention as cse/skills/scout/youtube_rss.py — no API key required). LEADERBOARDS SECTION (schema_version 2, additive — existing consumers only read 'sources'): the top-level 'leaderboards' array registers NUMERIC score sources — living leaderboard/eval websites harvested for score snapshots conforming to score-schema.json. Each entry is an INDEPENDENT best-effort rung: enabled entries are all attempted per run, a failed fetch/parse NEVER aborts the run, and every attempt (fetched | parsed | failed + snapshot_count) is recorded in the run's source_health_report (see score-schema.json). Per-entry fields: id (slug, becomes score_snapshot.source_slug), kind 'leaderboard', name, url, stance_hint (always 'independent_eval' for leaderboards), enabled (flip to false to skip a rung without deleting it), benchmark_slugs (default benchmark_slug mappings for snapshots harvested here), metrics (expected metric+unit hints), parse_hints (how to extract numbers from this living website — JS-heavy pages may need the r.jina.ai reader fallback), and note.

sources.name: Anthropic News
sources.note: Anthropic's release/announcement page — model cards, launch posts, headline benchmark claims for the Claude family.

sources.name: OpenAI Blog
sources.note: OpenAI's news page — GPT release announcements, system cards, and first-party eval claims.

sources.name: Google DeepMind Blog
sources.note: Google DeepMind's blog — Gemini release posts and research announcements.

sources.name: Meta AI Blog
sources.note: Meta AI's blog — Llama release posts and open-weights announcements.

sources.name: Theo (t3dotgg)
sources.note: Working engineer's hands-on takes on new models and dev tooling — fast, opinionated, builder-perspective reactions to releases.

sources.name: AI Explained
sources.note: Careful independent analysis of model releases and benchmark claims — runs own evals (e.g. SimpleBench), scrutinizes lab papers and leaderboard validity.

sources.name: Matthew Berman
sources.note: High-volume hands-on model testing and AI news coverage — informal test suites and early practitioner impressions of new releases.

leaderboards.name: LMArena
leaderboards.parse_hints: Arena Elo table keyed by model name — map display names to canonical model_slugs. The page is JS-heavy (client-rendered table); a plain fetch may return no numbers, so fall back to the r.jina.ai reader (https://r.jina.ai/https://lmarena.ai/leaderboard) and parse the rendered text table. Best-effort: if neither yields numbers, record 'failed' in the source_health_report and move on.
leaderboards.note: Crowd-sourced pairwise preference arena — the de-facto Elo signal for overall and per-category (coding/writing) model preference.

leaderboards.name: Artificial Analysis
leaderboards.parse_hints: Model comparison tables/charts with throughput (output tokens/sec), blended price (USD per 1M tokens), and their Intelligence Index. JS-heavy dashboard — prefer the r.jina.ai fallback (https://r.jina.ai/https://artificialanalysis.ai/models) to get rendered text, then extract per-model rows. Record price and speed as separate snapshots per model.
leaderboards.note: Primary feed for the 'speed' and 'cost_efficiency' capability axes — independent throughput/latency measurements plus normalized pricing, alongside their aggregate intelligence index.

leaderboards.name: SWE-bench Leaderboard
leaderboards.parse_hints: Leaderboard tables per split (Verified / full / Lite) listing system+model entries with '% Resolved'. Map the Verified tab to benchmark_slug 'swe-bench-verified' and the full split to 'swe-bench'. Entries are often scaffold+model combos — record the scaffold in the snapshot's 'harness' field and map the underlying model to model_slug. If the table is client-rendered, use the r.jina.ai fallback.
leaderboards.note: The headline real-world coding benchmark — resolved-rate on real GitHub issues; primary numeric feed for the 'coding' axis. Harness-sensitive: always capture the scaffold caveat.

leaderboards.name: Aider Polyglot Leaderboard
leaderboards.parse_hints: Static docs page with an HTML table: model name, 'Percent completed correctly' (record as metric 'accuracy'), edit format, and cost. Usually parseable from a plain fetch without the r.jina.ai fallback. Record the edit format (e.g. 'diff', 'whole') in the snapshot's 'harness' field; the cost column can optionally feed cost context notes.
leaderboards.note: Practical multi-language code-editing benchmark from the aider project — a strong independent 'coding' axis signal that often diverges from SWE-bench rankings.

leaderboards.name: ARC Prize / GPQA Reporting Pages
leaderboards.parse_hints: ARC Prize leaderboard lists per-system ARC-AGI accuracy (map to benchmark_slug 'arc-agi'); use the r.jina.ai fallback if the table is client-rendered. GPQA (map to 'gpqa-diamond') rarely has one canonical living leaderboard — numbers usually surface via lab announcement/eval report pages, so parse those best-effort and set the snapshot's source_url to the actual report page. Note cost-per-task or compute tier in 'harness' when ARC discloses it.
leaderboards.note: Frontier reasoning feeds for the 'reasoning' axis — ARC-AGI (novel-problem generalization) plus GPQA Diamond (graduate-level science) gathered best-effort from prize and report pages.
